raw_segments.text: Mrs. Page._, There is an old tale goes that Herne the Hunter, Sometime a keeper here in Windsor Forest, Doth all the winter time, at still midnight, Walk round about an oak, with great rag'd horns. Thirty and there he blasts the tree, and takes the cattle, and makes milch-kind yield blood, and shakes a chain in a most hideous and dreadful manner. You have heard of such a spirit, and well you know the superstitious idle-headed elders thirty-five receiv'd, and did deliver to our age, this tale of Herne the Hunter for a truth.
